paragraphs: BorgWarner Inc. (collectively with its consolidated subsidiaries, the "Company" or "BorgWarner") is a Delaware corporation incorporated in 1987. The Company is a global product leader in clean and efficient technology solutions for combustion, hybrid and electric vehicles. BorgWarner's products help improve vehicle performance, propulsion efficiency, stability and air quality. The Company manufactures and sells these products worldwide, primarily to original equipment manufacturers ("OEMs") of light vehicles (passenger cars, sport-utility vehicles, vans and light trucks). The Company's products are also sold to OEMs of commercial vehicles (medium-duty trucks, heavy-duty trucks and buses) and off-highway vehicles (agricultural and construction machinery and marine applications). The Company also manufactures and sells its products to certain tier one vehicle systems suppliers and into the aftermarket for light, commercial and off-highway vehicles. The Company operates manufacturing facilities serving customers in Europe, the Americas and Asia and is an original equipment supplier to nearly every major automotive OEM in the world.

The Company's current strategy is to focus on profitable growth across its technology-focused product portfolio that supports electric, hybrid and combustion vehicles. This entails growing its product portfolio through organic investments and technology-focused acquisitions. The Company's balanced portfolio is particularly critical as the automotive industry continues to see electric vehicle adoption volatility across different regions. During the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, the Company's revenue from eProducts, which include all products utilized on or for electric vehicles ("EVs") plus those same products and components that are included in hybrid powertrains whose underlying technologies are adaptable or applicable to those used in or for EVs, was approximately $2.6 billion, $2.3 billion and $2.0 billion, respectively, or 18%, 17% and 14% of its total revenue, respectively, and the Company's revenue from Foundational products, which include all products utilized on internal combustion engines plus those same products and components that are also included in hybrid powertrains, was approximately $11.7 billion, $11.8 billion and $12.2 billion, respectively, or 82%, 83% and 86% of its total revenue, respectively.

Acquisitions have been an integral component of the Company's growth and value creation strategy. Refer to Note 2, "Acquisitions and Dispositions," to the Consolidated Financial Statements in Item 8 of this report for more information, including a summary of recent acquisitions.
Refer to Note 24, "Reportable Segments and Related Information," to the Consolidated Financial Statements in Item 8 of this report for financial information about the Company's reportable segments.

The Company discloses segment information under four reportable segments, consistent with the way operating results are evaluated by management: Turbos & Thermal Technologies, Drivetrain & Morse Systems, PowerDrive Systems and Battery & Charging Systems. The sales information presented above does not include the sales by the Company's unconsolidated joint ventures (see sub-heading "Joint Ventures" below). Such unconsolidated sales totaled approximately $764 million, $764 million, and $732 million for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.

Turbos & Thermal Technologies develops and manufactures products to improve fuel economy, reduce emissions and enhance performance. Turbos & Thermal Technologies' technologies include turbochargers, eBoosters, eTurbos, emissions systems, thermal systems, gasoline ignition technology, smart remote actuators, powertrain sensors, cabin heaters, battery heaters and battery cooling systems.

Turbos & Thermal Technologies' emissions, thermal and turbocharger systems provide several benefits, including increased power for a given engine size, improved fuel economy, reduced emissions and optimized temperatures in propulsion systems and vehicle cabins. Sales of turbochargers for light vehicles represented approximately 21%, 21% and 22% of the Company's net sales for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively. No other single product line accounted for more than 10% of consolidated net sales in any of the years presented.

Turbos & Thermal Technologies' powertrain products include an array of highly engineered products that complement and enhance the efficiency improvements delivered by many other air management technologies.

Drivetrain & Morse Systems' technologies include hydraulic controls, friction and mechanical clutch products for automatic transmissions and torque-management products. Additionally, Drivetrain & Morse Systems' products include chain systems as well as variable camshaft phasing products.

Drivetrain & Morse Systems' friction and mechanical products for automatic transmissions include dual clutch modules, friction clutch modules, electromagnetic clutches, friction and separator plates, transmission bands, torque converter clutches, one-way clutches and torsional vibration dampers. Hydraulic controls products for automatic transmissions feature electro-hydraulic solenoids for standard and high-pressure hydraulic systems, transmission solenoid modules and dual clutch hydraulic control modules.

Our business success depends on attracting and retaining qualified personnel.
Our profitability and results of operations may be adversely affected by new business launch difficulties.

Work stoppages, production shutdowns and similar events could significantly disrupt our business.
Our benefit plan expenses and obligations may fluctuate depending on various factors, including changes in interest rates, changes in regulations and plan asset returns.

Our operations may be affected by greenhouse emissions and climate change and related regulations.

paragraphs: Investors should carefully consider the following risk factors and other information included in this report. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial also may impact our business operations. If any of the following risks occur, our business, including our financial performance, financial condition, operating results and cash flows, could be adversely affected. In such an event, the market price of our common stock could decline, and you could lose all or part of your investment.

Our strategy is to focus on profitable growth across our technology-focused product portfolio that supports electric, hybrid and combustion vehicles by growing our eProducts as well as continuing our focus on Foundational products. Our balanced portfolio is particularly critical as the automotive industry continues to see electric vehicle adoption volatility across different regions.

We may not prove successful in our strategy due to many factors, including any of the risks identified in the paragraphs that follow, failure to develop new products that our customers will purchase, technology changes that could render our products obsolete, or the introduction of new technology to which we do not have access, among other things.

Our future success is dependent upon us making the right investments at the right times, with the right customers who can rapidly adapt to the market, to support product development in areas of evolving vehicle technologies. We have made, and expect to continue to make, significant investments to grow our eProducts. If the overall adoption of electric vehicles continues to be slower as compared to our expectations, we may not only fail to realize expected rates of return on our existing investments, we may also incur further losses on such investments. Further, if we invest in relationships with the wrong customers or in the wrong markets, then we may still fail to realize expected returns.

We expect to continue to pursue business ventures, acquisitions, and strategic alliances that leverage our technology capabilities and enhance our customer base, geographic representation, and scale to complement our current businesses. We regularly evaluate potential growth opportunities. While we believe that such transactions are an integral part of our long-term strategy, there are risks and uncertainties related to these activities. Assessing a potential growth opportunity involves extensive due diligence. However, the amount of information we can obtain about a potential growth opportunity can be limited, and we can give no assurance that past or future business ventures, acquisitions, and strategic alliances will positively affect our financial performance or will perform as planned. Assessing a price for potential transactions is inexact.

As noted, we conduct certain of our operations through joint ventures, where we may share ownership and management responsibilities with one or more partners that may not share our goals and objectives. Operating a joint venture may require additional organizational formalities as well as the sharing of information and decision making with our partners. Additional risks associated with joint ventures include one or more partners failing to satisfy contractual obligations, the ability to enforce such obligations, conflicts arising between us and any of our partners, a change in the ownership of any of our partners and less of an ability to control compliance with applicable rules and regulations, including the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act and related rules and regulations.

The Company operates manufacturing facilities serving customers in Europe, the Americas and Asia and is an original equipment supplier to nearly every major automotive OEM in the world.

The Company's current strategy is to focus on profitable growth across its technology-focused product portfolio that supports electric, hybrid and combustion vehicles. This entails growing its product portfolio through organic investments and technology-focused acquisitions. The Company's balanced portfolio is particularly critical as the automotive industry continues to see electric vehicle adoption volatility across different regions. During the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, the Company's revenue from eProducts, which include all products utilized on or for electric vehicles ("EVs") plus those same products and components that are included in hybrid powertrains whose underlying technologies are adaptable or applicable to those used in or for EVs, was approximately $2.6 billion, $2.3 billion and $2.0 billion, respectively, or 18%, 17% and 14% of its total revenue, respectively, and the Company's revenue from Foundational products, which include all products utilized on internal combustion engines plus those same products and components that are also included in hybrid powertrains, was approximately $11.7 billion, $11.8 billion and $12.2 billion, respectively, or 82%, 83% and 86% of its total revenue, respectively.

On September 19, 2024, the Company commenced a lawsuit against PHINIA, seeking to recover from PHINIA approximately $120 million of value added tax ("VAT") refunds that PHINIA received or expects to receive from governmental agencies as well as damages and interest. These refunds consisted of VAT paid by the Company in periods prior to or directly related to the spin-off that established PHINIA as an independent company. PHINIA responded to the lawsuit and also asserted counterclaims against the Company. On October 15, 2025, the Company entered into a settlement agreement (the "Settlement Agreement") with PHINIA, pursuant to which PHINIA agreed to pay the Company $78 million, resolving the lawsuit and certain other matters relating to the spin-off. In connection with the Settlement Agreement, the Company and PHINIA also entered into an amended and restated tax matters agreement that, among other things, limits the Company's responsibility to certain defined tax obligations. As a result, the Company recorded a net charge of $40 million during the year ended December 31, 2025, for the reduction of VAT-related receivables, the elimination of certain Company liabilities under the amended and restated tax matters agreement and related legal fees, which is included in Other operating expense, net in the Company's Consolidated Statements of Operations. As of December 31, 2025, after giving effect to the Settlement Agreement and the $31 million payment received during the fourth quarter of 2025, the Company had assets related to these VAT refunds of approximately $47 million included in Receivables, net in the Company's Consolidated Balance Sheet in Item 8 of this report.

In February 2025, the Company made the decision to exit its charging business within the Battery & Charging Systems reportable segment. Production operations ceased during the second quarter of 2025. This decision was made following the Company's continuing evaluation of its product portfolio and future investments. This action was intended to create a more focused portfolio and is expected to eliminate approximately $30 million of annualized adjusted operating losses by 2026. Refer to Note 2, "Acquisitions and Dispositions," to the Consolidated Financial Statements in Item 8 of this report for more information.

The Company also made the decision to consolidate its North American battery systems business, which is expected to align the business' cost structure to current market dynamics. This action is expected to result in annual cost savings of approximately $20 million by 2026.

On September 26, 2024, a hurricane made landfall in North Carolina disrupting operations at the Company's facility in Arden, North Carolina (the "Arden Plant"). The Arden Plant was largely untouched, but the Company experienced some loss or damage to the Company's assets amounting to less than $10 million. The Arden plant resumed full operations during the fourth quarter of 2024. The Company's insurance policies (less applicable deductibles) covered the repair or replacement of the Company's assets that incurred loss or damage and provided coverage for interruption to its business, including lost profits, and reimbursement for other expenses and costs that were incurred related to the damages and losses sustained. For the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company recorded committed insurance recoveries of approximately $9 million, which are included as a reduction of Cost of sales in the Company's Consolidated Statements of Operations in Item 8 of this report and were fully collected.

Acquisitions have been an integral component of the Company's growth and value creation strategy. Refer to Note 2, "Acquisitions and Dispositions," to the Consolidated Financial Statements in Item 8 of this report for more information, including a summary of recent acquisitions.

Economic Conditions. The Company's financial performance depends on conditions in the global automotive industry. Automotive and truck production and sales are cyclical and sensitive to general economic conditions and other factors, including interest rates, consumer credit and consumer spending and preferences. Government policies, such as the imposition of, termination of or other changes in tariffs (including retaliatory tariffs), or the commencement or termination of consumer tax incentives, such as EV tax credits and programs to invest in infrastructure, including EV charging stations, may affect consumer preferences. Economic declines or impacts of tariffs that result in a material reduction in automotive or truck production would have an adverse effect on the Company's sales. The weighted average market production, as estimated by the Company for the year ended December 31, 2025, was approximately flat from the year ended December 31, 2024. Weighted average market production reflects light and commercial vehicle production as reported by S&P Global, weighted for the Company's geographic exposure, as estimated by the Company.

Commodities and Other Inflationary Impacts. During 2025, prices for commodities showed a lower level of volatility in comparison to what the Company had experienced from the beginning of 2021. The Company expects commodities and other costs to be relatively flat in 2026. However, the Company has experienced impacts from commodity pricing, inflation and tariffs over the last several years. Volatility in these areas and other factors could cause actual costs to be materially higher than expected in 2026.

The Company expects global industry production to be flat to down modestly year-over-year in 2026. The Company expects a negative sales impact from declining sales in the Company's Battery & Charging Systems segment. As a result, at the mid-point of its outlook, the Company expects total sales in 2026 to decline year-over-year, excluding the impact of foreign currencies.

The Company maintains a positive long-term outlook for its global business and is committed to new product development and strategic investments to enhance its product leadership strategy. There are several trends that are driving the Company's long-term growth that management expects to continue, including adoption of product offerings for electrified vehicles and increasingly stringent global emissions standards that support demand for the Company's products that drive vehicle efficiency.

A detailed comparison of the Company's 2023 operating results to the Company's 2024 operating results can be found in the Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations section in the Company's 2024 Annual Report on Form 10-K filed February 6, 2025.

paragraphs: BorgWarner Inc. (包含其合併子公司在內，簡稱 "本公司" 或 "BorgWarner") 為一間設立於1987年的德拉瓦州公司。本公司為全球清潔且高效能科技解決方案的領導者，應用於內燃機、混合動力與電動車輛。BorgWarner 的產品有助於提升車輛性能、驅動效率、穩定性與空氣品質。本公司在全球製造與銷售這些產品，主要銷售對象為輕型車輛（轎車、休旅車、貨車與輕型卡車）的原廠設備製造商（"OEMs"）。本公司產品亦銷售至商用車輛（中型貨車、重型貨車與巴士）與非道路車輛（農業與建設機械及船用應用）的原廠設備製造商。本公司亦製造與銷售產品至某些一級車輛系統供應商，以及輕型、商用與非道路車輛的後市場。本公司經營服務於歐洲、美洲與亞洲客戶的製造廠，並為全球幾乎所有主要汽車原廠設備製造商的原廠設備供應商。

本公司的現行策略為著重於其科技導向產品組合的獲利成長，以支持電動、混合動力與內燃機車輛。此策略包含透過內生投資與科技導向併購來擴充其產品組合。本公司的平衡產品組合在汽車產業持續面臨不同地區電動車採用波動的同時，尤為關鍵。在截至2025年12月31日、2024年12月31日及2023年12月31日的會計年度中，本公司來自eProducts的收入，包含所有應用於或用於電動車輛（"EVs"）的產品，加上相同產品與零組件，這些產品與零組件亦包含於混合動力系統，其基礎技術可適應或應用於電動車輛的技術，約為26億美元、23億美元與20億美元，分別佔總收入的18%、17%與14%；而來自Foundational產品的收入，包含所有應用於內燃機的產品，加上相同產品與零組件，這些產品與零組件亦包含於混合動力系統，約為117億美元、118億美元與122億美元，分別佔總收入的82%、83%與86%。

Turbos & Thermal Technologies 開發與製造產品，以提升燃油經濟性、減少排放並增強性能。Turbos & Thermal Technologies 之技術包括渦輪增壓器、eBoosters、eTurbos、排放系統、熱能系統、汽油點火技術、智慧遙控執行器、動力總成感測器、車室加熱器、電池加熱器及電池冷卻系統。

Turbos & Thermal Technologies 之排放、熱能及渦輪增壓系統提供多項好處，包括在相同引擎尺寸下提升動力、改善燃油經濟性、減少排放，以及最佳化動力系統與車室溫度。輕型車輛用渦輪增壓器銷售佔本公司淨銷售額約為 2025 年 12 月 31 日財務年度終結時 21%、2024 年 12 月 31 日財務年度終結時 21% 以及 2023 年 12 月 31 日財務年度終結時 22%。任何一年度中，無其他單一產品線佔合併淨銷售額超過 10%。
Turbos & Thermal Technologies 之動力總成產品包含一系列高度工程化產品，可補強並提升許多其他空氣管理技術所帶來的效率改善。
Drivetrain & Morse Systems 之技術包括自動變速箱用液壓控制、摩擦與機械離合器產品以及扭力管理產品。此外，Drivetrain & Morse Systems 之產品亦包含鏈條系統以及變換氣門正時產品。
Drivetrain & Morse Systems 之自動變速箱用摩擦與機械產品包括雙離合模組、摩擦離合模組、電磁離合器、摩擦與分離板、變速箱帶、扭力變換器離合器、單向離合器以及扭振減震器。自動變速箱用液壓控制產品包含標準與高壓液壓系統用電液線圈、變速箱線圈模組以及雙離合液壓控制模組。

paragraphs: BorgWarner Inc. (包含其合併子公司，以下稱為 "本公司" 或 "BorgWarner") 是全球在清潔且高效能科技解決方案的產品領導者，應用於內燃機、混合動力及電動車輛。BorgWarner 的產品有助於提升車輛性能、動力效率、穩定性及空氣品質。本公司製造並銷售這些產品至全球各地，主要銷售給輕型車輛（轎車、休旅車、貨車及輕型卡車）的原廠製造商（"OEMs" )。本公司產品也銷售給商用車輛（中型貨車、重型貨車及巴士）及非道路用車輛（農業及建設機械與船用應用）的原廠製造商。本公司亦製造並銷售其產品至部分一級車輛系統供應商，以及輕型、商用及非道路用車輛的後市場。本公司經營的製造設施服務於歐洲、美洲及亞洲的客戶，並為全球幾乎所有主要汽車 OEM 原廠製造商提供原廠零件。

本公司目前的策略為聚焦於其科技導向產品組合的獲利成長，以支持電動、混合動力及內燃機車輛。這包括透過內生投資及科技導向併購來擴充其產品組合。本公司平衡的產品組合在汽車產業持續觀察電動車採用波動性的情況下，尤為關鍵。在截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日、2024 年 12 月 31 日及 2023 年 12 月 31 日的會計年度，本公司來自 eProducts 的營業收入，包含所有用於或針對電動車（"EVs"）的產品，加上相同產品及零組件，這些零組件也包含在混合動力系統中，其底層技術可適應或應用於電動車，約為 26 億美元、23 億美元及 20 億美元，分別佔總營業收入的 18%、17% 及 14%。本公司來自 Foundational 產品的營業收入，包含所有用於內燃機的產品，加上相同產品及零組件，這些零組件也包含在混合動力系統中，約為 117 億美元、118 億美元及 122 億美元，分別佔總營業收入的 82%、83% 及 86%。

2024 年 9 月 19 日，本公司對 PHINIA 提起訴訟，要求 PHINIA 支付約 1.2 億美元的增值稅（"VAT"）退款，這些退款為 PHINIA 從政府機關取得或預期取得的，以及損害賠償及利息。這些退款為本公司在 PHINIA 獨立公司設立前或直接相關期間所支付的增值稅。PHINIA 對訴訟作出回應，並對本公司提出反訴。2025 年 10 月 15 日，本公司與 PHINIA 籤訂和解協議（"和解協議"），根據該協議，PHINIA 同意支付本公司 7,800 萬美元，解決訴訟及與分拆相關的其他事項。根據和解協議，本公司與 PHINIA 也簽訂修正後的稅務事項協議，該協議限制本公司對某些特定稅務義務的責任。因此，本公司於截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日的會計年度，因減少與增值稅相關的應收款、消除修正後稅務事項協議下的某些本公司負債及相關法律費用，而計入其他營運費用，淨費用為 4,000 萬美元。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，考慮到和解協議及 2025 年第四季收到的 3,100 萬美元付款後，本公司在財務報表第 8 項中，於應收款淨額內，與這些增值稅退款相關的資產約為 4,700 萬美元。

2024 年 9 月 19 日，本公司對 PHINIA 提起訴訟，要求 PHINIA 支付約 1.2 億美元的增值稅（"VAT"）退款，這些退款為 PHINIA 從政府機關取得或預期取得的，以及損害賠償及利息。這些退款為本公司在 PHINIA 獨立公司設立前或直接相關期間所支付的增值稅。PHINIA 對訴訟作出回應，並對本公司提出反訴。2025 年 10 月 15 日，本公司與 PHINIA 籤訂和解協議（"和解協議"），根據該協議，PHINIA 同意支付本公司 7,800 萬美元，解決訴訟及與分拆相關的其他事項。根據和解協議，本公司與 PHINIA 也簽訂修正後的稅務事項協議，該協議限制本公司對某些特定稅務義務的責任。因此，本公司於截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日的會計年度，因減少與增值稅相關的應收款、消除修正後稅務事項協議下的某些本公司負債及相關法律費用，而計入其他營運費用，淨費用為 4,000 萬美元。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，考慮到和解協議及 2025 年第四季收到的 3,100 萬美元付款後，本公司在財務報表第 8 項中，於應收款淨額內，與這些增值稅退款相關的資產約為 4,700 萬美元。
2025 年 2 月，本公司決定退出 Battery & Charging Systems 應報告分部內的充電業務。生產作業於 2025 年第二季停止。此決定係基於本公司持續評估其產品組合及未來投資。此舉旨在建立更聚焦的產品組合，預期於 2026 年可消除約 3,000 萬美元的年度調整營運虧損。有關更多資訊，請參閱本報告第 8 項「合併財務報表」所附的附註 2，「收購與處置」。
本公司亦決定將其北美電池系統業務進行合併，預期可使該業務的成本結構與現行市場動態一致。此舉預期於 2026 年可實現約 2,000 萬美元的年度成本節省。

2024 年 9 月 26 日，颱風在北卡羅來納州登陸，造成本公司位於北卡羅來納州阿登（Arden Plant）廠區的運作中斷。阿登廠區幾乎未受損壞，但本公司遭受部分資產損失或損害，總計低於 1,000 萬美元。阿登廠區於 2024 年第四季恢復全額運作。本公司保險政策（扣除適用免賠額後）已覆蓋本公司遭受損失或損害的資產之修復或更換，並提供對本公司業務中斷的保障，包括損失利潤，以及與損害及損失相關的其他費用和成本之補償。於 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年終結，本公司已確認約 9,000 萬美元的保險賠償，此金額已列為本公司合併營運損益表（第 8 項「合併財務報表」）中成本銷售的減項，且已全部收取。
收購一直是本公司成長與價值創造策略的重要組成部分。有關更多資訊，請參閱本報告第 8 項「合併財務報表」所附的附註 2，「收購與處置」，包括近期收購的總結。

總體經濟狀況。本公司的財務表現取決於全球汽車產業的狀況。汽車及貨車的生產與銷售具有週期性，且對總體經濟狀況及其他因素，包括利率、消費者信貸與消費支出及偏好，較為敏感。政府政策，例如關稅（包括報復性關稅）的課徵、終止或其它變動，或消費者稅 incentives 的啟動或終止，例如電動車稅抵免及投資基礎設施的計畫，包括電動車充電站，可能影響消費者偏好。經濟衰退或關稅的影響導致汽車或貨車生產大幅減少，將對本公司的銷售產生不利影響。本公司預估 2025 年 12 月 31 日財年終結的加權平均市場生產量，與 2024 年 12 月 31 日財年終結的加權平均市場生產量大致持平。加權平均市場生產量反映 S&P Global 報告的輕型及商用車生產量，並根據本公司地理風險敞口進行加權，為本公司預估的結果。
原物料及其他通貨膨脹影響。2025 年，原物料價格的波動程度較本公司自 2021 年初以來所經驗到的為低。本公司預期 2026 年原物料及其他成本將相對持平。然而，本公司在過去幾年已經驗到原物料價格、通貨膨脹及關稅的影響。這些領域的波動性及其他因素，可能導致 2026 年實際成本大幅高於預期。
本公司預期 2026 年全球產業生產量將與去年相比持平或小幅下滑。本公司預期因 Battery & Charging Systems 分部銷售下滑，將對銷售產生負面影響。因此，在展望的中點，本公司預期 2026 年總銷售額將與去年相比下降，不計外幣影響。
本公司對其全球業務持正面的長期展望，並致力於新產品開發及戰略投資，以強化其產品領導策略。有幾個趨勢正在推動本公司長期成長，管理階層預期這些趨勢將持續，包括電動車產品的採用，以及日益嚴格的全球排放標準，這些標準支持對本公司產品的需求，以提高車輛效率。
本公司 2023 年營運成果與 2024 年營運成果的詳細比較，可參閱本公司 2024 年年報（Form 10-K）中「管理層對財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析」部分，該年報於 2025 年 2 月 6 日提交。

與我們產業相關的風險
汽車產業的狀況可能對我們的業務產生負面影響。
我們面臨強烈的競爭。
若我們未能適當回應，汽車產業的演進可能對我們的業務產生負面影響。
本公司可能面臨政府機構針對車輛排放標準所進行之調查及相關程序。
與本公司業務相關之風險
本公司承受來自原廠（OEMs）大幅壓縮我們產品價格之壓力。
本公司持續面臨用以生產產品之原物料成本波動，以及通貨膨脹率高漲之情況。
本公司可能無法實現部分或全部預期之重整計畫效益，且重整行動可能對本公司業務產生負面影響。
本公司面臨資訊科技（"IT"）系統日益集中化所導致之業務持續性風險。
資訊科技基礎建設之失敗或中斷，包括與網路安全相關之中斷，可能對本公司業務及營運產生負面影響。
本公司業務之成功取決於吸引並留住合適之人才。
本公司之獲利能力及營運成果可能因新業務啟動困難而受到不利影響。
本公司部分員工為工會所組織，此情形可能使本公司面臨罷工之風險。
罷工、生産停擺及其他類似事件可能對本公司業務造成重大幹擾。
本公司之福利計畫費用及義務可能因多種因素而波動，包括利率變動、法規變更及計畫資產回報等。
本公司需遵守嚴格之環境法規，且這些法規可能變更，並伴隨重大風險。
本公司之營運可能受溫室氣體排放及氣候變遷及其相關法規之影響。
本公司已遭受到並持續面臨與環境、產品保固、產品回收、訴訟及其他聲請相關之責任。
本公司偶爾會涉及法律程序及商業或契約爭議，此等情形可能對本公司業務造成不利影響。
遵守及法律變更可能導致成本增加，並可能影響我們的營運成果。
稅法或稅率的變更，以及稅務機關的稅務稽查結果，可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。
我們面臨與國際業務相關的風險。
我們在中國的業務面臨激烈的競爭，且對經濟、政治及市場條件變化較為敏感。
我們的債務評級 downgrade 可能限制我們取得債務資本市場的資本能力。
與我們客戶相關的風險
我們對主要客戶的勞動關係影響較為敏感。
與我們供應商相關的風險
我們可能因供應商無法提供零組件而遭受供應不足的影響。
供應商的經濟困境可能導致供應中斷，進而幹擾我們的營運，並對我們的業務造成不利影響。
我們可能面臨財務交易對手無法償付債務的風險。
與 PHINIA Inc. 分拆相關的風險。
PHINIA Inc. 的分拆可能無法實現預期的稅務好處，並可能使我們面臨額外的稅務風險。
根據 PHINIA Inc. 分拆而產生的潛在責任，可能對我們的業務造成重大且不利的影響。
多種其他因素可能對我們的業務造成不利影響。
paragraphs: 投資人應謹慎考量下列風險因素及其他資訊，包含於本報告中。其他未目前為我們所知或目前認為不重要的風險與不確定性，也可能影響我們的業務運作。如果任何下列風險發生，將可能對我們的業務，包括財務表現、財務狀況、營運成果與現金流產生不利影響。在這種情況下，本公司普通股的市場價格可能下跌，投資人可能損失全部或部分投資。
我們的策略是專注於透過支援電動車、混合動力車與傳統內燃機車的科技導向產品組合，實現獲利成長，同時擴大我們的 eProducts 並持續著重於 Foundational 產品。我們的平衡產品組合在汽車產業持續觀察不同地區電動車採用波動性時，尤為關鍵。
我們可能無法成功實現此策略，原因包括但不限於後續段落中所識別的任何風險、未能開發客戶會購買的新產品、科技變革可能使我們的產品過時，或新科技的出現而我們無法取得，以及其他因素。
我們未來的成功取決於我們在正確的時間、與能迅速適應市場的正確客戶進行正確的投資，以支持演進中的車輛科技的產品開發。我們已進行，並預期持續進行，重大投資以擴大我們的 eProducts。如果電動車整體採用速度持續慢於我們預期，我們不僅可能無法實現對現有投資的預期回報率，也可能在這些投資上產生進一步的虧損。此外，如果我們投資與錯誤的客戶或錯誤的市場，我們仍可能無法實現預期的回報。

我們預期持續追求能運用我們科技能力、擴大客戶羣、地理覆蓋範圍與規模，以補強我們現有業務的業務合作、收購與戰略聯盟。我們定期評估潛在的成長機會。雖然我們認為這些交易是我們長期策略的重要組成部分，但這些活動也伴隨著風險與不確定性。評估潛在成長機會需要進行廣泛的盡職調查。然而，我們能取得有關潛在成長機會的資訊可能有限，我們無法保證過去或未來的業務合作、收購與戰略聯盟會對我們的財務表現產生正面影響，或會按計畫執行。評估潛在交易的價格是不確定的。
如前所述，我們透過合資企業進行部分業務運作，我們可能與一個或多個夥伴共同擁有與管理責任，這些夥伴可能不與我們有相同的目標與宗旨。經營合資企業可能需要額外的組織程序，以及與夥伴分享資訊與決策。與合資企業相關的額外風險包括一個或多個夥伴未能履行契約義務、執行這些義務的能力、我們與任何夥伴之間產生的衝突、任何夥伴的股權變動，以及較難控制符合適用的法規與規則，包括《外國腐敗行為防治法》及相關法規與規則。
